findings.summary: The whole-criterion exemption on 'refus*/reject*/append*/amend*/supersede*' would let the cited 8gkv instance through, and the corpus case is invented wording, not the instance.
findings.evidence: HISTORY.txt:1095: commit 620c657 'Stop pending-check merge refusals firing D87; append note to decisions' touches the same files as the rejected 8gkv candidate (gh client, landing, transport, watcher, records.rs, decisions.md). D150 (decisions.md:4030) is titled 'Pending-check merge refusals no longer fire D87's signal'. A criterion from that job naturally contains 'refusals' (exempt via refus*) and 'append a note to D87' (exempt via append, and 'append'/'add'/'note' are not in the edit-verb list). The plan's case 'Edit the existing D87 entry in place...' is wording that does not reflect how the job described the change. Known-misses in Risks admit 'a bad criterion that adds the word refuse or append', but here those words are not a dodge; they are the topic's own vocabulary. Fix: Drop the whole-criterion exemptions. Treat a decision id as edited unless it is the object of 'amends/supersedes/cites' in a clause that introduces a new entry. Add 'append ... to Dnn', 'add a note to Dnn' and 'Dnn notes/says' as in-place edit forms when Dnn is an existing id. Add a refusing corpus case written from the real 8gkv/D150 wording (with 'refusals' and 'append a note to D87'), and keep the accept cases for 'append a new decision that amends D87'.
findings.location: Decision 2 (exemption words) and Demonstration for criterion 3 (case criterion-edits-existing-d87-entry-in-place)

findings.summary: Every command mentioned in backticks is treated as one the verifier must run. D43 judges only the commands a criterion cites as its evidence, so mentions of `cargo fmt --all` or `git commit` as behavior of the code under test are refused.
findings.evidence: D43 (decisions.md:968-974) judges the commands a behavior criterion cites as evidence against those the verifier ran. Athena's own format step runs `cargo fmt --all` then `cargo fmt --all --check` (crates/athena-core/src/run/format.rs:5,71). A criterion such as 'Run `cargo test -p athena-core format`: the step runs `cargo fmt --all` before `cargo fmt --all --check`' would be refused. So would a criterion for athena-git or commits.rs (commits.rs:6 mentions `git merge --ff-only`) that names a git write command as code behavior. The plan's own criterion 1 needs the 'refus*' exemption only because it mentions `cargo fmt` in backticks without asking anyone to run it. Fix: Read only the commands the criterion cites to run: the backticked commands in its leading 'Run `...`' clause (the form the corpus and reading.rs tests use), split into simple commands. Leave backticked mentions elsewhere in the text unread. Then remove the refus*/reject* exemption. Add accept tests for a criterion that mentions `cargo fmt --all` and `git commit` as behavior of the code under test.
findings.location: Decision 2 / Step 1 (commands read from every backticked span) and Risks bullet 1

findings.summary: A hand-kept denylist stands in for the rule D43 enforces, which is the capability's verifier grant. The grant is readable data and the reader already receives it.
findings.evidence: athena.toml:76 and :108 define verifier_commands (cargo build/check/test/clippy/fmt/run/metadata/tree; git status/diff/log/show; ls), and :75 says fmt only with --check. reading.rs:620-628 builds `verifier_can_run` from `describe_commands(&c.verifier_grant(jc).commands)` plus 'cargo fmt only with --check'. The denylist misses `gh pr create`, `cargo doc`, `cargo bench`, `curl`, `make` and `rm`, none of which the verifier may run. It would also be wrong for a repository whose grant differs (system facts: Athena is meant to work on any user's repository). Fix: Pass the verifier grant into the check from the production gate at reading.rs:722 as an Option, and refuse a cited command that the grant does not allow, plus fmt without --check. Replay and tests pass None and the command rule is skipped. If the signature change is too large for one run, say in D174 that the denylist is interim and add a test that ties its entries to athena.toml verifier_commands, so the two cannot drift apart.

findings.summary: The 7qht instance is assumed to be `cargo fmt` without --check; the snapshot has no records to confirm it.
findings.evidence: D115 (decisions.md:2707-2732) was prompted by job ta60, not 7qht. D116 lists 7qht only for a send-back. Nothing in the snapshot shows 7qht's offending criterion. Fix: Label that corpus case 'synthetic: the class of 7qht', or cite where the instance text came from; do not present it as the instance itself.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 3 (case criterion-requires-cargo-fmt-without-check attributed to job 20261024-045548-7qht)

findings.summary: It is ambiguous whether a bare decision id near a common verb ('change', 'update', 'fix', 'remove') triggers a refusal; if it does, ordinary criteria are refused.
findings.evidence: The edit-verb list includes change/changes/update/updated/fix/remove. Criteria such as 'CHANGELOG.md is updated to name D174' or 'the fix changes the behavior D43 describes' put a D-id within 4 words of such a verb. The refusal_corpus has no such text today (Grep found none), so the accept tests would not catch the over-match. Fix: Require the docs/decisions.md path (or the words 'decision entry') in the same clause as an existing id, and add accept tests for a D-id near update/fix/change in a criterion about another file.
findings.location: Decision 2 (decision-edit matcher: 'a decision id ... or an existing/in place phrase next to docs/decisions.md, with an edit verb within 4 words')

findings.summary: Two more tests that split `refusing_check` into step lines are not listed.
findings.evidence: reading.rs:4928 (check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope) and reading.rs:5410 (environment_reach_has_one_step_line) also split `pub fn refusing_check(`. Both check position relative to a named step, so a new last step does not affect them, and `cargo test -p athena-core` runs them. Fix: Add them to the dependents entry for completeness.
findings.location: Dependents, entry 'The text of refusing_check and of the check_reading_acceptance doc'

summary: The plan puts the fix where the reading names it: one new last `step!` in `refusing_check`. Its references exist. These include `refusing_check` at checks.rs:520-549, `check_criteria_evidence` at surveys.rs:91, `gate_refuser` at reading.rs:7206, the corpus extractor at refusal_corpus.rs:2877 and `INPUT_FORMS` at [&str; 63], plus READING_RULES [&str; 12] and the baseline of 3045 bytes. A last position changes no existing ordering test, and the D174 and decision-links plan fits the guards. The approach fails the soundness test in three ways. (1) The exemption words ('refus*', 'reject*', 'append*', 'amend*', 'supersede*') apply to the whole criterion. They would exempt the very instance being prevented: HISTORY.txt:1095 shows that task as "Stop pending-check merge refusals firing D87; append note to decisions". (2) Every backtick span is read as a command the verifier must run, so a criterion that only mentions a command is refused, for example one about Athena's own `cargo fmt --all` format step. The 'refus*' exemption exists mainly to paper over this. (3) The forbidden commands are a hand-kept denylist, while the rule D43 enforces is the capability's verifier grant (athena.toml verifier_commands), which the reader brief already receives. Fix these three and the plan is acceptable.
